_comment: Historical keeper rounds were computed by hand. Entries here are accepted engine-vs-history divergences, keyed 'year:player name', each with a reason.

_categories.collision-order: Two keepers priced at the same round. The rules sheet does not say which one moves; the engine breaks the tie deterministically (years kept, then earlier basis, then alphabetical). History used the other order. Both engine and history occupy the SAME set of rounds — only the assignment differs.
_categories.flag-gap: The Sleeper is_keeper flag on an earlier pick does not match what the hand sheet tracked. The downstream rounds only reconcile if that pick was a keep. 2021 is the league's first flagged draft (2020 has 150 picks and zero flags).
_categories.hand-math: The rules-as-written produce a different round than the sheet recorded, with no collision or traded pick to explain it. Hand-computed era.
_categories.unresolved-rule: AMBIGUOUS — see the report. Whether the consecutive-keep counter is player-scoped or team-scoped is not settled by the written rules. The engine's current reading (player-scoped) is left unchanged pending the league owner's ruling; these two rows are recorded, not endorsed.

entries.2022:Allen Lazard: collision-order. Roster 1 kept Lazard + Bateman, both FA basis, both priced at round 10; the pair occupied rounds 9 and 10 in history exactly as the engine does, only swapped (engine's alphabetical tiebreak gives Lazard 10 / Bateman 9; the draft recorded Bateman 10 / Lazard 9). Rules do not specify who moves.
entries.2022:Rashod Bateman: collision-order. Mirror of 2022:Allen Lazard — same roster-1 round-10 collision, same {9,10} pair, opposite assignment.
entries.2022:Courtland Sutton: hand-math / FA treatment. Sutton was drafted 2021 r6 by roster 5; the rules set basis = round in the most recent draft, so his first keep for roster 11 costs 5 (6-1). The sheet listed him at round 10, the flat FA-pickup slot, i.e. it treated the mid-season acquisition as an undrafted pickup. History charged the owner 5 rounds MORE than the rules required, so this is not a negotiated discount. Note 13 of the 17 roster-change keepers in 2022-2025 were correctly charged prior-round-minus-1, so this is an isolated row, not a rule.
entries.2022:Jakobi Meyers: collision-order (cascade). Roster 11 kept three players at rounds 10/9/8: Sutton, Meyers, Darrel Williams. Meyers' engine cost is correct (2021 r11 - 1 = 10); the recorded 9 falls out of the three-way round-10 collision once Sutton is (wrongly, see 2022:Courtland Sutton) also priced at 10. Engine and history use the same round set {8,9,10}.
entries.2022:Darrel Williams: collision-order (cascade). True FA (no prior draft pick anywhere in 2020-2021), cost 10, third man in the roster-11 round-10 pileup; history put him at 8, the engine at 9. Same {8,9,10} round set.
entries.2022:Justin Jefferson: flag-gap + collision-order. Roster 7 drafted Jefferson 2020 r15 and picked him again 2021 r14 — exactly the first-keep price, same roster — but that 2021 pick carries no is_keeper flag. Reading 2021 as a keep, 2022 costs 14-4 = 10, collides with Joe Burrow (2021 r11 - 1 = 10), and round 8 was traded away, so the loser of the collision slides to 9: exactly the recorded Jefferson 9 / Burrow 10. Reading the flag as written (engine) gives 13, which nothing in the draft explains. Corroborated downstream: Jefferson was NOT keepable in 2024 and re-entered the draft, which only holds if 2021+2022+2023 were three consecutive keeps.
entries.2023:Justin Jefferson: flag-gap. Same missing 2021 keeper flag as 2022:Justin Jefferson. Third consecutive keep off his recorded 2022 round: 9-8 = 1, exactly the recorded round 1. The engine, counting only the flagged 2022 keep, charges 9-4 = 5.
entries.2023:Keenan Allen: flag-gap / chain not reset. Allen went 2020 r5 (roster 3) -> 2021 r4 keeper (roster 3) -> 2022 r3 by roster 11, recorded as a plain draft pick at exactly the first-keep price -> 2023 r1. The recorded 1 is 3-4 floored, i.e. the sheet counted 2023 as his SECOND consecutive keep; the engine resets the count on the 2022 non-keeper pick as rule 5 requires and charges 3-1 = 2. Round 2 was owned and unoccupied, so no collision forced round 1.
entries.2023:Joe Burrow: hand-math. Burrow was kept by roster 7 in 2022 (r10) and again in 2023, so the rules charge the second-keep offset: 10-4 = 6. The sheet recorded 9 = 10-1, the FIRST-keep offset. Roster 7 traded no picks that year and round 6 was owned and unoccupied, so nothing forced the slide — and 9 costs the owner 3 rounds more than the rules require, ruling out a negotiated discount.
entries.2023:Ja'Marr Chase: hand-math. 2021 r5 (real pick) -> 2022 r4 keeper -> 2023 second consecutive keep = 4-4 = 0, floored to round 1 by rule 3. The sheet recorded round 2. Roster 9 traded no picks and its round 1 was owned and unoccupied; three other 2023 keepers league-wide (Diggs, Higgins, Allen) did land on round 1, so there is no unwritten 'keepers cannot occupy round 1' rule — the floor was simply applied one round short.
entries.2022:Rhamondre Stevenson: hand-math. Drafted 2021 r13 by roster 6; kept by roster 2 in 2022. Rules: basis = most recent draft round, so 13-1 = 12, and roster 2 owned round 12 (it spent that pick normally). The sheet recorded round 10, the flat FA slot — same misreading as 2022:Courtland Sutton, and again 2 rounds more expensive than the rules required.
entries.2023:Rhamondre Stevenson: hand-math. Off his recorded 2022 round of 10 the second keep costs 10-4 = 6, and with roster 2's rounds 5 and 6 traded away the engine slides him to 4. The sheet recorded 8. Neither the iterative rule (6, or 4 after the slide) nor the recorded-round chain produces 8; 8 equals 12-4, i.e. the sheet appears to have kept subtracting from a standing basis of 12 (the nominal 13-1 it never actually used in 2022). Continuation of the mis-tracked row above.
entries.2024:Rhamondre Stevenson: hand-math. Third year of the same mis-tracked row: off his recorded 2023 round of 8 the third keep is 8-8 = 0, floored to 1 (rounds 1-3 all owned and free). The sheet recorded 4 = 12-8, again consistent with a standing basis of 12 rather than the iterative rule the rest of the league follows.
entries.2024:Jerome Ford: collision-order. Roster 1 kept Ford + Kyren Williams, both true FAs with no prior draft pick, both priced at round 10; engine assigns Ford 10 / Kyren 9 on the alphabetical tiebreak, the draft recorded Kyren 10 / Ford 9. Identical {9,10} round set; the rules do not say who moves.
entries.2024:Kyren Williams: collision-order. Mirror of 2024:Jerome Ford — same roster-1 round-10 FA collision, opposite assignment.
entries.2025:Baker Mayfield: collision-order. Roster 11 kept Mayfield + Bucky Irving, both FA basis (Mayfield's last draft pick was 2021; he was undrafted in 2024, so basis = FA per rule 1), both priced at round 10; engine assigns Mayfield 10 / Irving 9, the draft recorded Irving 10 / Mayfield 9. Same {9,10} round set.
entries.2025:Bucky Irving: collision-order. Mirror of 2025:Baker Mayfield — same roster-11 round-10 FA collision, opposite assignment.
entries.2022:Stefon Diggs: unresolved-rule. Diggs was kept by roster 2 in 2021 (r5, his first keep off a 2020 r6 pick), then changed rosters and was kept by roster 8 in 2022 at r4 = 5-1, the FIRST-keep offset. The engine, counting keeps player-scoped as rule 5 is written, charges the second-keep offset 5-4 = 1. Round 1 was owned and free, so nothing forced 4. Recorded, not endorsed — see the ambiguity note in the report.
entries.2023:Diontae Johnson: unresolved-rule. Second and only other instance of the same pattern: kept by roster 4 in 2021 (r12) and 2022 (r8), then changed rosters and was kept by roster 5 in 2023 at r7 = 8-1, the FIRST-keep offset, where player-scoped counting makes it a third keep at 8-8 floored to 1. Roster 5 traded no picks and rounds 1-6 were all free. Two for two on roster-change keepers with zero counterexamples in 2022-2025 — hence a rule question, not a math slip. Recorded, not endorsed.
